Rashi on Shabbat 63a:10:1.hebrew: ופליגא - הא דקתני ״בטלין לימות המשיח״, פליגא דשמואל, דלשמואל אין בטלין לימות המשיח:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:10:1.english: And [this] disagrees - That which [the baraita] teaches, "[they] are obsolete in the days of the Messiah," disagrees with Shmuel, for according to Shmuel they are not obsolete in the days of the Messiah.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:10:2.hebrew: לא יחדל - משמע לעולם, אלמא יש עניות ועשירות. ש"מ: נחמות שנתנבאו הנביאים — ״ולא יהיה כנעני עוד״ (זכריה י״ד:כ״א) — לא לימות המשיח נתנבאו, שהן מן העולם הזה; דאם כן, חדל לך אביון:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:10:2.english: Will not cease - This implies forever; thus, there is poverty and wealth [even then]. Conclude from this: The consolations that the prophets prophesied — [such as,] “nor shall there be a merchant any more” (Zechariah 14:21) — were not prophesied for the days of the Messiah, for they are [part] of this world; for if so, the pauper would have ceased for you.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:11:1.hebrew: מסייע ליה - ברייתא דקתני בטלין לימות המשיח, לרבי חייא בר אבא:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:11:1.english: [This] supports him - The *baraita* that taught "[they] are eliminated in the messianic era" [supports] Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:11:2.english: Did not prophesy - [This refers to] their words of consolation.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:11:3.english: No eye has seen - The eye of the prophets had no power to see it.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:14:1.hebrew: בדברי תורה כתיב - הוי זהיר לחזר על משנתך, שתהא מזומנת לך בשעת הדין להביא ראיה, כחרב על ירך גבור לנצח במלחמה. והוא הודך והדרך:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:14:1.english: It is written in reference to matters of Torah - Be careful to review your learning, so that it will be ready for you at the time of judgment to bring proof, like a sword on the thigh of a warrior to triumph in battle; and that is “your glory and your majesty.”

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:15:1.hebrew: דליגמר איניש - לגרוס שמעתא מרביה, ואף על גב דלא ידע לכולהו טעמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:15:1.english: That a person should learn - To recite teachings from his teacher, even though he does not know all their reasons.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:15:2.hebrew: והדר ליסבר - טעמיה. דהא קשה ליה לרב כהנא, ולא הוה ידע להאי טעמא, ותלמודיה הוה קים ליה מדהוה בר תמני סרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:15:2.english: And then understand - Its rationale. For this was difficult for Rav Kahana and he did not know this reason, yet his learning was firmly established for him from when he was eighteen [years old].

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:17:1.hebrew: המחדדין - שואלין ומשיבין, ולא לקפח, אלא להתחדד:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:17:1.english: Who sharpen - They ask and answer [each other], and not to defeat [one another], but rather to be sharpened:

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:17:2.english: And your majesty - [Is] like veḥadedkha [and He will sharpen you].

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:17:3.english: And let it teach you - And it will teach you.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:18:1.hebrew: עושר וכבוד ליכא - בתמיה: כיון דאיכא אורך ימים, כ"ש עושר וכבוד:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:18:1.english: There are no riches and honor? - [This is asked] in astonishment: Since there is length of days, all the more so [there are] riches and honor.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:18:2.hebrew: למיימינין - של תורה, שמפשפשין טעמיהן בדקדוק ובוררין, כימין המיומנת למלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:18:2.english: To those who use the right hand - [In matters] of Torah: who scrutinize their reasons with precision and clarify [them], like the right [hand], which is skilled for work.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:18:3.hebrew: למשמאלין בה - שאין יגעים בה כל צרכן. אי נמי: מיימינין בה — עוסקין לשמה, משמאילים — שלא לשמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:18:3.english: To those who relate to its left - Who do not labor in it as much as is needed. Alternatively: "Those who relate to its right" — they engage [in it] for its own sake; "those who relate to its left" — not for its own sake.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:19:1.hebrew: הנוחין זה לזה - נושאין ונותנין בה בנחת רוח, מתעסקין כדי שילמדו זה מזה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:19:1.english: Who are agreeable to each other - They deliberate over it pleasantly, engaging [in study] in order to learn from one another.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:19:2.hebrew: ידבר עמים תחתינו - ישפיל, וכל שפלות בנחת. ל"א: הנוחין — מנהיגין זה את זה להבנתה של הלכה, כמו ״לך נחה״ (שמות ל״ב:ל״ד); ״ידבר״ — תרגום של ״ינהג״:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:19:2.english: “He subdues peoples under us” - [It means] He lowers [them]; and all lowering is [conducted] with gentleness. Another explanation: [The word] hanochin [“who are agreeable” means that] they guide one another toward the understanding of the halakha, as in: “Go, lead” (Exodus 32:34); [and] yadber is the [Aramaic] translation of yanheg [“he will guide”].

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:1:1.hebrew: ביין חרדלי - שחור, כלומר: לבנה או שחורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:1:1.english: On mustard[-colored] wine - Black [wine]; that is to say: a fair or dark[-complexioned woman].

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:1:2.hebrew: במסב רחב - מיסב — מטה שמיסב עליה בשעת אכילה, ולענין ניאוף — אשה שמנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:1:2.english: On a wide couch - A meisav is a couch upon which one reclines at the time of eating, and with regard to adultery — a plump woman.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:1:4.english: A good friend - A good-looking woman.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:22:1.english: And who may say to Him: What do You do? - One who observes commandments can say to Him.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:23:1.hebrew: המקשיבין - מלמדים זה את זה ומבינים זה מזה, ולישנא דקרא נקט:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:23:1.english: Who listen - They teach one another and understand from one another; and [the sage] employed the phrasing of the verse.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:23:3.hebrew: חבירים מקשיבים - זה לזה. להם אני אומר שישמיעוני קולם, ואענם:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:23:3.english: The companions heed - [That is, they listen] to each other. To them I say: Let them make Me hear their voice, and I will answer them.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:24:1.english: Run away, my beloved - It is written after it [the previous verse].

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:25:1.hebrew: המדגילים - מאספין זה את זה, ואומרים: ״בא ונלמוד ונבין בין שנינו, הואיל ואין לנו רב ללמדנו״:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:25:1.english: Who assemble - They gather one another and say: “Come, let us study and understand between the two of us, since we have no teacher to teach us.”

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:25:2.hebrew: צורתא - שורש הדבר, קצת למדו מרבם:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:25:2.english: The form - The root of the matter — they learned a little from their teacher.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:26:1.english: Greater is one who lends - Because the poor person is not embarrassed by the matter.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:26:2.hebrew: ומטיל לכיס - מעות ומלאי, להשתכר בהן למחצית שכר. ואיידי דאיירי רבי אבא אמר ריש לקיש, נקט כל הני מילי דאגדתא דאמר להו ר' אבא משמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:26:2.english: And one who places into a purse - [He provides] money and merchandise to earn profit with them for half of the profit. And since [the Gemara] was dealing with [teachings that] Rabbi Abba said [in the name of] Reish Lakish, it cited all these aggadic matters that Rabbi Abba said in his name.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:27:1.hebrew: חוגרו - הדבק בו, שסופך ליהנות מתלמודו:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:27:1.english: Gird him - Cleave to him, for you will ultimately benefit from his Torah study.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:27:2.hebrew: אל תדור בשכונתו - שאינו יודע בדקדוקי מצות, ואין חסידותו שלם, וסופך ללמוד ממנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:27:2.english: Do not dwell in his neighborhood - For he is not knowledgeable in the precise details of the commandments, and his piety is not complete, and you will ultimately learn from him.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:28:1.english: Prevents kindness - For he does not allow the poor to come to his door.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:28:2.english: “To him that is afflicted” [lamas] - That is, a dog.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:2:1.english: Of Tzimtzemai the queen - That was her name.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:3:1.hebrew: באלה - מפרש בגמ': קולפא — מצוק"ה בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:3:1.english: With an alla - It is explained in the Gemara: kulpa — macuge in Old French [a club].

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:5:1.hebrew: וכתתו חרבותם - ואי תכשיטין נינהו, לא יהו בטלין לעתיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:5:1.english: And they shall beat their swords - And if they were ornaments, they would not be eliminated in the future.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:6:1.english: A garter - It is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:6:2.english: Is pure - It does not contract ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:6:3.hebrew: ויוצאין בה - דלא שלפא ומחויא, שלא יראה שוקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:6:3.english: And she may go out with it - For she will not remove [it] and show [it], so that her leg will not be seen.

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:7:1.english: Ankle chains are ritually impure - In the Gemara, it explains this:

Rashi on Shabbat 63a:9:1.hebrew: שרגא בטיהרא - נר בצהרים. מתוך שאינו צריך, אינו נאה; אבל בזמן הזה, שהוא עת מלחמה — תכשיטין הן:
Rashi on Shabbat 63a:9:1.english: A candle in the afternoon - A lamp at midday. Since it is not needed, it is not attractive; but in the present time, which is a time of war, they are ornaments.

Tosafot on Shabbat 63a:10:1.hebrew: אין בין העוה"ז לימות המשיח - אע"ג דהשתא אין ירושלים ואין בהמ"ק, ואילו לימות המשיח יהיה הכל בנוי — צ"ל דהאי "אין בין" לאו דוקא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 63a:10:1.english: "There is no difference between this world and the days of the Messiah" - Even though now there is no Jerusalem and no Temple, whereas in the days of the Messiah everything will be rebuilt, one must say that this [phrase], "there is no difference," is not exact.
